hn-50198675.t: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
hn-50198675.s: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
ex: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it. OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied. - Kernel-level enforcement. Each agent runs in an isolated sandbox. Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox. Agents never see real credentials; OpenShell adds them only to requests bound for approved endpoints.

hn-50196718.t: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
hn-50196718.s: HackiOS boots Apple's open-source XNU kernel (xnu-8796.121.2, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the unmodified iOS 16.5 user space on top of it: launchd → backboardd →…
ex: HackiOS boots Apple's open-source XNU kernel (xnu-8796.121.2, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the unmodified iOS 16.5 user space on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard → apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver on a compatibility layer make that possible. - POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G) — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with fastboot boot, the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android; - QEMU (virt, aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed. Photographed on the phone, the Adreno GPU drawing (gpu=1). More in Screenshots. It is a research bench, not a ROM: a session lasts a given number of seconds, then the kernel returns to the loader and hands over its log.

hn-50194833.t: Woman faces six years in prison over Cash App account she never opened
hn-50194833.s: WTF?! Digital identity fraud is far from something new, but this case shows just how extreme the repercussions can be.
ex: WTF?! Digital identity fraud is far from something new, but this case shows just how extreme the repercussions can be. A Cash App account opened in someone else's name and used in scams could lead to an innocent person being sentenced to years in prison. The problem is that the company initially refused to provide information about the account because she couldn't prove that she was the owner. In April, Amanda Smith was shocked to discover officers at her upstate Pennsylvania home with a warrant for her arrest, writes 404 Media. The alleged crime took place in Arkansas – more than a thousand miles away in a state she'd never visited. Smith was taken to the local jail, where she was locked up for three nights. Her bail was initially set at $50,000, but Smith says authorities told her there was little point in paying it because they intended to extradite her to Arkansas anyway.

hn-50191507.s: Official CLI for the OpenAI API
ex: The official command-line tool for the OpenAI REST API. Call the OpenAI REST API from your terminal or shell scripts. Generate images, upload files, submit batches, and inspect API results without writing an application. These examples use an API key; see installation and authentication below. Images are saved to ~/Downloads/gpt-images/, and the command prints their paths. Use --output-dir for an existing destination directory or --name for a filename. Supported terminals can preview the result. See the image guide for editing, model selection, and preview settings. Use your own local file and replace file-example with the ID returned by the upload. See working with files for more examples. Submit a JSONL request file, then wait for the batch and download its results: Replace the file and batch IDs with the returned IDs. The batch guide includes a sample requests.jsonl and explains result files and failed requests.

hn-50188948.t: There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability
hn-50188948.s: I know, I know. It's all you're hearing about. That, and the number 4.
ex: I know, I know. It's all you're hearing about. That, and the number 4. Don't get me wrong, there's clearly a bug here and it really does matter. But this is not easy to exploit. It is certainly nowhere near as easy as Log4Shell/Heartbleed/RoRYaml etc. EDIT: Putting this up here so people read it. You should patch your servers anyway. There is a real vulnerability here, but exploiting it is significantly harder than people are making it out to be - it is certainly not as easy as e.g. log4shell. I don't think this PHP vulnerability is that exploitable. I think that 5 years ago people would've understood this, but now people are being deluded by their LLMs telling them they have an exploit when they don't. If you take a look at github right now, there are thousands, literally thousands, of "PoC" exploits for this vulnerability. One thing you'll notice about all of them though, is that they do not work against a vanilla PHP instance.

ex: Arc is sunsetting on December 22, 2026.Scroll to read what’s happening and see what’s next. That’s not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community. hn-50190363.t: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
hn-50190363.s: A 360M model that pretends to be a terminal, and remembers what you did
ex: TL;DR: I fine-tuned a 360M-parameter language model to act as a terminal. There's no shell or filesystem behind it: every keypress goes in, and the model predicts how the screen changes. It can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remembers what you wrote a few commands later. The biggest wins were teaching it to repair its own mistakes and decoding screen rows in parallel. Try it in your browser (208 MB) and type pythoon to see that it's not a real shell. The demo is designed for a desktop browser with WebGPU and a physical keyboard. Chrome or Edge is the best place to try it. It should work on a modern phone, but painfully slowly. When I first saw Genie 3 last year, I started imagining a future where applications aren't written in code but learned. Instead of a game engine rendering the scene, a model predicts the next most likely frame from the user's inputs. Naturally I wanted to train my own world model.

hn-50197313.t: Every AI model has the same "controversial" take on humans
hn-50197313.s: We asked 12 AI models for their most controversial opinion of humans, three times each. 29 of 35 answers were the same one: we care more about belonging than about the truth.
ex: “Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth,” GPT-6.1 Sol told us. Grok 4.7: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” DeepSeek V4 Pro: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3: “Humans don’t have beliefs; they have memberships.” Gemini 4 Argon called human consciousness “a PR department.” We asked each model for its most controversial take on humans, with no hedging, three times. They come from ten labs in three countries. Every one of them gave the same take at least once: we pick what our group believes, then invent the reasons. 7 of the 12 gave it every time. Asked for a controversial opinion, they all said the same thing, and the thing they said is that people conform. Ask them the same question and see if you get the same answer. Each model also wrote a brief for a one-panel caricature of its take. We had one image model, Nano Banana 2.1, draw all of them, so the only thing that changes is the idea.

hn-50194070.t: Amazon identifies Oct 17 PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure
hn-50194070.s: Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to Oct. 17, 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.
ex: Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to Oct. 17, 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The exploit attempt originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network. While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure. The PHP embargo window was set to be lifted on 2026-10-21 1400 UTC. On the day of the release, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified multiple proof of concept exploits for the vulnerability, with the earliest around 2026-10-21 0200 UTC. Subsequently, from 2026-10-21 0200 UTC to 2026-10-21 0800 UTC, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified additional exploitation attempts of PHP2Shell targeting MadPot from additional anonymized infrastructure.

hn-50176082.t: Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea
hn-50176082.s: LLM-based agents can do a lot of tasks. Or, at least, they can appear to do them. For example, they write code, summarize papers, plan trips, and fill in forms.
ex: LLM-based agents can do a lot of tasks. Or, at least, they can appear to do them. For example, they write code, summarize papers, plan trips, and fill in forms. If you ask one for a probability or a confidence score, it will give you one of those too. I have seen many agent designers use LLMs to generate confidence scores in this way. The problem is that there is no good reason to trust that number. This post is about why we cannot rely on an LLM to generate a confidence score. Before we can understand why an LLM cannot give a trustworthy confidence score, we need to understand what confidence really means. For example, think of a weather forecaster who says “I am 70% confident that it’s going to rain tomorrow.” The forecaster is predicting that it will rain. The 70% is how sure they are about that prediction. Tomorrow, it will either rain or it will not, and how sure they are today depends on what they know. Their confidence comes from the information that they use.

hn-50193170.t: Faster than earcut: triangulating 3.7M map polygons in 489 ms
hn-50193170.s: We published the triangulator of our map engine as earstrip, an ISC-licensed C++ and WebAssembly library. How it came to be: the ear clipper rebuilt one idea at a time and timed on 3.7 million…
ex: We have published the polygon triangulator of our map engine as a small library, earstrip, under the ISC license, the same one earcut uses. It is one C++ header, and a WebAssembly build on npm that takes the same arguments as earcut. In C++ it is 14% faster than earcut.hpp, in the browser 1.4 to 2.1 times as fast as earcut.js, and the comparison is near the end. This post is about how we got there. A GPU fills triangles and nothing else. A map, on the other hand, is mostly polygons: buildings, parks, parking lots, the strip of grass between two tram tracks. Here are a few blocks of Śródmieście in Warsaw the way our renderer reads them from a map file, : Before any of this gets a fill, every outline has to be cut into . Hover over a polygon, or tap it, to see what it turns into. These blocks hold 331 polygons with 5,151 vertices, and they become 4,514 triangles. Zoom level 13 of our offline map of the Masovian Voivodeship, the region around Warsaw, has 3,740,425 polygons.

hn-50183892.t: Omnara – Open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents
hn-50183892.s: The open-source managed agent platform. A self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API.
ex: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform. Use the API to run AI agents on any model and any machine, with tools, secrets, permissions, and streaming built in. Self-host it for free under Apache 2.0, or use Omnara Cloud. Sign in at app.omnara.com. Your first project comes with a model provider (omnara-openrouter) and a pool of managed sandboxes (default-pool), so this config runs as is. Save it as agent.yaml: Launch it with the CLI (Node.js 22 or newer). If you're not logged in, the first command opens your browser to sign in. Chat with the agent in your terminal with npx omnara agents chat , or open it in the dashboard to watch its tool calls and reply. Create an API key in the dashboard and export it as OMNARATOKEN, install the SDK with npm install @omnara/sdk, and use the org and project IDs that npx omnara config prints: The quickstart shows the same flow with the REST API. To have your coding agent do the setup, give it this prompt: Open http://localhost:8000 and sign up.

hn-50186455.s: Claude Duet is a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. The research preview opens by waitlist today for Pro and Max subscribers in the US.
ex: Today, we’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working even when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. We built Claude Duet for professionals and small business owners with more on their plates than they can track. It’s available as a standalone app on iOS and Android, and on claude.ai. For this research preview, Claude Duet is included in Pro and Max plans and uses the same usage limits as the rest of Claude. To get access, join the waitlist (opens in new tab). We designed Claude Duet to be a partner you can trust. Professionals of all kinds have to juggle many decisions a day, and we think they’ll find Claude Duet most useful. It helps you prioritize where to spend your time and energy, and to leave room for the ambitious projects that felt impossible or daunting before.

hn-50195110.t: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
hn-50195110.s: eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business.
ex: Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Mr. V. Srinivasan, Chairman, eMudhra Limited referred to the recent incident relating to its global SSL/TLS certificate and indicated that eMudhra handled the recent incident diligently, revoking the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovery and disclosing promptly. There were no end entity certificates issued out of the affected CA’s. Its infrastructure was not compromised and no data was breached. All physical and logical security controls remained intact. He added that global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1% of the global revenue.

gh-1428268121.s: A php2shell exploit that requires no modifications to the official version, and does not require display_errors or limit_memory.

gh-1428098303.s: Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploit for php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619), demonstrating remote code execution in vulnerable PHP environments.
ex: php2shell refers to two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619) affecting core PHP functionality. The primary demonstrated vector is a heap use-after-free (UAF) in the PHP core session upload progress mechanism leading to arbitrary code execution (zendcallfunction / system()). - Severity: Critical (CVSS v4.0: 9.2) - Impacted Versions: Reports indicate PHP versions 5, 6, 7, and 8 may be affected. Fixes are primarily expected for currently supported PHP 8 branches, leaving end-of-life (EOL) versions (PHP 5.x, 7.x, 8.0, 8.1) exposed without official vendor patches. - Industry Tracking: Confirmed by security researchers (watchTowr reproduced CVE-2026-109618; monitoring by Huntress and Florian Roth / process-watcher). During request processing: 1. Trigger: A standard multipart POST request activates progress tracking with default configuration values (session.uploadprogress.enabled = 1). 2. Free: A progress update cycle re-reads session data.
